candidateConcepts.rationale: A structured examination of an incident or close call to understand what happened, why it happened, and what must change to prevent recurrence.
An incident that could have caused injury or illness but did not; also called a near miss.
A method that looks beyond the worker action nearest the event to program, design, planning, organizational, equipment, training, and operational factors.
Protecting and documenting relevant physical conditions before evidence is disturbed so the investigation can reconstruct what occurred.
Systematic collection of observations, interviews, documents, logs, records, photographs, and other information needed to establish the event sequence and contributing conditions.
The direct or readily visible condition or action associated with an incident, which may be a symptom rather than the underlying system failure.
A fundamental underlying system-related reason an incident occurred that identifies a correctable failure.
A structured analysis used to move beyond immediate causes and identify the underlying systemic reasons that allowed an incident or near miss to occur.
A condition, event, decision, action, or system weakness that contributed to how an incident developed and that may help reveal root causes.
A chronological reconstruction of relevant events and conditions used to understand sequence, interactions, missing information, and causal relationships.
An action that addresses an identified cause or program deficiency so the same or a similar incident is less likely to recur.
Follow-up that checks whether an implemented corrective action actually controls the identified problem and prevents recurrence rather than merely closing the action administratively.

crossCompetencyReferences.reason: Corrective actions may be organized in an action plan, but the generic Action Plan concept is canonical in D02 C02.
OSHA lists logic/event trees as possible root-cause tools, but the generic system-safety Event Tree concept belongs with D02 C06.
Worker involvement strengthens investigations, but the generic participation concept is canonical in D02 C03.
Investigation findings support organizational learning, but the generic learning concept is canonical in D02 C03.
